texts: A sternal wound infection after CABG is best prevented by decolonising Staphylococcus aureus before surgery: intranasal mupirocin and skin decontamination with an antiseptic soap such as chlorhexidine.
Most deep sternal infections come from the patient's own staphylococci, often carried in the nose.
Prophylactic antibiotics should stop within 48 hours; keeping them while the drains are in place breeds resistance without reducing infection.
Vancomycin in place of cefazolin, or an added aminoglycoside, is not the best preventive measure for most patients.
In the picture, the mop scrubs the hidden golden grapes out of the nose and the lavender soap lathers the stern spotless.
Memory hook: a mop in the nose and soap on the skin keep the mould away.
